questions.q: What is ASFF, as described in this lesson?
options: A GuardDuty-only severity scale running from 0.1 to 8.9
A CLI tool for configuring Security Hub
The AWS Security Finding Format -- a normalized schema Security Hub returns findings in, regardless of which source (GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, third-party) generated them
An IAM policy type used to grant read access to findings
questions.explain: ASFF is the AWS Security Finding Format: the consistent backbone of fields (Severity, Resources, Workflow.Status, etc.) that Security Hub normalizes every finding into, no matter its source.

questions.q: Why does the lesson's Security Hub example use securityhub.get_paginator("get_findings") instead of calling get_findings() directly in a loop?
options: Paginators abstract away each AWS API's own token-based pagination shape, so the same for-loop pattern works across services
get_findings() does not accept a Filters argument
Pagination is only needed when there are zero findings
get_paginator() is required before boto3 will authenticate
questions.explain: boto3 paginators exist because every paginated AWS API has its own token field and shape; the paginator lets you write the same 'for page in paginator.paginate(...)' loop regardless of the underlying service.

questions.q: How does retrieving GuardDuty findings differ from retrieving Security Hub findings, per this lesson?
options: GuardDuty findings cannot be retrieved with boto3 at all
GuardDuty findings do not use ASFF
Security Hub requires a DetectorId while GuardDuty does not
GuardDuty requires a two-step pattern: list_findings() returns only finding IDs, then get_findings() fetches the full finding objects for those IDs
questions.explain: GuardDuty splits retrieval into list_findings() (IDs matching FindingCriteria) and get_findings() (full objects for a batch of IDs), unlike Security Hub's single get_findings() call.

questions.q: What does guardduty.list_detectors()["DetectorIds"][0] rely on, according to this lesson?
options: That GuardDuty findings are always sorted by severity
That a region has at most one GuardDuty detector, making the first (and only) detector ID safe to grab this way in a single-detector-per-region account
That Security Hub and GuardDuty share the same detector ID
That list_detectors() always returns an empty list in production accounts
questions.explain: A region can have at most one GuardDuty detector, so taking DetectorIds[0] is a safe pattern in a typical single-detector-per-region account.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against comparing an ASFF Severity.Normalized score directly against a GuardDuty native severity value?
options: Because they're on two different numeric scales -- ASFF Normalized runs 0-100, while GuardDuty's native severity runs 0.1-8.9 -- and need to be mapped onto one common scale before correlating
Because GuardDuty severities are always higher than ASFF severities
Because ASFF severities are text-only and have no numeric form
Because GuardDuty findings never include a severity field
questions.explain: ASFF's Normalized score (0-100) and GuardDuty's own native severity scale (0.1-8.9) are different ranges; the lesson recommends mapping both onto one common scale before comparing or correlating them.
